budget_note: Parent-proposed (the owner did not set a strict cap). Planned 40; extended to 45 after wave 2 produced 14 candidates so every candidate gets Phase 3 and Phase 5 verification. Three critic-2 units deferred for budget. Owner raised the cap to 50 and then 60 in the resuming session (Phase 3 re-runs, Phase 5 one verifier per record).
execution_note: Agent-run target code (pure-function harnesses, unit tests) runs only through the parent's sbx wrapper: docker run --network none --read-only, host /usr and target mounted read-only, writes only to agents/<id>/scratch, uid 65534, cap-drop ALL, no-new-privileges, 512 MiB memory, 1 CPU, 64 pids, 32 MiB file size, 120 s wall clock, explicit env allowlist (HOME, TMPDIR, PATH, PYTHONPATH, PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE, PYTHONNOUSERSITE). Checks that need the real Docker-backed control plane (sandbox containers, desktop image) are run by the parent with dummy principals in a scratch AGENTBOX_HOME on loopback inside this disposable cloud container, as the owner requested; such checks are labelled parent-live in the ledger. Promotion uses the parent-side promote.py (no-follow dir_fd walk, single-link regular files, 256 KiB per file, 1 MiB per agent).

new_unvalidated_leads.summary: An allowlisted exec such as 'tail -f /dev/null & ' x1100 fills the sandbox pids cgroup; bash then fails to fork and exits 254 before GNU timeout fires, so the group kill never happens and ~1000 uid-1000 tail processes stay. The sandbox remains at pids.max after the exec returns (even a root docker exec pkill could not run), which also keeps GUI-burst collection failing (v09).
